answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with unique biometric commitments. Each identity binds itself to one human through a hashed, privacy-preserving biometric template, and the network rejects any second identity using the same template. A farm cannot mint copies, because each fake needs a distinct living person, and people cannot be copied or rented in bulk. Like a harbor at dawn, each identity arrives once and is seen; a ripple from one person cannot pretend to be many. Each extra fake needs its own distinct human, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
